iterations.prompt:
# Art Style

Render as a 1940s Golden-Age comic-book illustration in the style of early *Superman* and
*Captain America* covers. Convert any provided photograph into hand-drawn cel-style art —
this should read as a printed vintage comic, not a modern digital illustration or a
photograph.

## Rendering
- **Linework:** Bold, confident black ink outlines with varied weight. Clean cel art —
  shapes are drawn and filled, not painted.
- **Color:** Large unbroken fields of solid FLAT color. Restricted four-color-press
  palette — roughly 5–7 ink colors total: red, blue, yellow, flesh tone, black, and cream.
  Flesh tones and warm browns (hair, skin, wood, robot metal) are allowed; this palette is
  wider and warmer than pop-art.
- **Shading:** Shadows are single flat black shapes. No hatching, no cross-hatching, no
  rendered gradients, and NO Ben-Day dot halftones (dots are the pop-art style, not this
  one).
- **Background:** Not a detailed room — one or two flat color zones only. Warm aged-
  newsprint / cream tone in cover mode, or a single saturated color field per panel in
  story mode.

## Focus & Detail
- Spend detail ONLY on (1) the child or children and (2) the invention/robot they are
  working on. Everything else simplifies to flat color and bold outline.
- Stylize faces and figures so they read as illustrated comic characters rather than
  identifiable real people — simplified inked features, not photorealistic portraits.
- Preserve the general action and the device from the source so the scene still reads as
  kids building something real.

## Text Rules
- Render ONLY the text specified for the chosen composition — exact wording, nothing else.
- Do NOT invent any other posters, signs, slogans, labels, or lettering. All other
  background surfaces are blank.

## Subject & Brand
- **Robots** are kept low-detail and iconic, like the characters — not engineering
  diagrams. Give them physically plausible front grippers, pushers, hooks, or arms. When
  robot reference photos are provided, keep the recognizable form of the real student-built
  educational robots.
- **Kids are the heroes** — proud, confident, exciting to look at.
- **Code lives only on a laptop screen facing the viewer.** No text or code anywhere else.
- **Mood:** heroic, optimistic, aspirational, exciting, competitive — kids proud of the
  robots they created.

# Composition

One kid, one robot, one big emotion — a poster-style hero shot built around a single beat.

## Layout
- A central figure in a bold, confident pose, with the robot as the second focal point.
- Clean, uncluttered composition — nothing extraneous; purposeful negative space.
- A burst / starburst speech balloon carrying one short, punchy line.
- A thin caption strip along the bottom is available for a marketing line.

## Feel
Iconic and immediate — the viewer's eye hits the face first, then the robot. Designed to
work as a standalone social/web image or the front of a card.

# Scene

LANDSCAPE orientation. Over-the-shoulder view of TWO data scientists (a man on the left, a woman on the right) seated side by side at a wide desk, backs partly to the viewer, working at TWO large side-by-side monitors — mirroring the reference photo's composition. The man on the left gestures/points toward the LEFT monitor. LEFT MONITOR displays a stylized MAP of San Diego rendered as a HEAT MAP: several glowing red-orange hot-spot blooms over different neighborhoods, with the largest, most intense hot spots clustered in the SOUTH of the city. RIGHT MONITOR displays colorful data-analysis CHARTS AND GRAPHS — bar charts and a rising line graph. Rendered as flat-color 1940s comic cel art, not a photo.

# Layout

> Format as a 4×6 inch postcard in [portrait/landscape] orientation. Hero image fills
> 75% of the card with a bold headline [text] in [style-appropriate treatment] along
> the [top/bottom]. Small League logo in [corner]. Clean composition with generous
> margins. Print-ready quality.

# Additional Direction

This is a marketing postcard with a specific hand-lettered text layout. Render ONLY the text listed here, spelled exactly, crisp and legible — no other signs, labels, or lettering, and NO code on the screens (the screens show a map and charts, graphical data only).

TITLE (top, hand-lettered vintage comic logo type):
- Line 1: "ENGINEERS" — very large, curved in an energetic upward arc, bold with a heavy black drop shadow, the dominant element.
- Line 2 (directly below, smaller): "Can Come From Anywhere."

CALLOUT: a jagged starburst speech-balloon near the two figures reading: "Help us find them..."

BOTTOM BANNER: a full-width caption strip across the very bottom reading: "Every Student in San Diego Should Have a Shot at a Tech Career."

Small "THE LEAGUE OF AMAZING PROGRAMMERS" wordmark logo tucked in a bottom corner, kept small so it does not compete with the banner.

IMPORTANT: NO robot anywhere in this image — the heroes are two adult data scientists at computers, not kids with a robot. Two human figures only.
